advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Narrow the 'consumed' exemption so only `.get`/subscript (value-scoped) receivers are sanctioned, not value-rendering methods like `.copy`/`.items`/`.values`.
evidence: `if isinstance(sub, (ast.Attribute, ast.Subscript)) and _is_os_environ(sub.value): consumed.add(id(sub.value))` (lines 67-68) marks os.environ safe as the receiver of ANY attribute, e.g. `.copy`
Docstring line 12: `os.environ.get("X")` and `os.environ["X"]` assertions are SAFE: only the retrieved value is an operand — but `.copy()`/`.items()`/`.values()` retrieve/render ALL values
Module docstring even names `.copy()` and `{**os.environ}` as env-construction leak shapes, yet the assert detector would not flag `assert x == os.environ.copy()`
advisory.finding: The assert-route detector `_bare_environ_nodes` sanctions `os.environ` whenever it is the receiver of any attribute access, including `os.environ.copy()`, `os.environ.items()`, and `os.environ.values()`. The results of those calls repr the full set of environment VALUES (secrets) on assertion failure, so `assert x == os.environ.copy()` would leak the whole environment yet the detector reports zero findings — contradicting the module's stated purpose.
scenarios: A future test writes `assert extracted == os.environ.copy()` or `assert (k,v) in os.environ.items()`; the audit stays green while a failure dumps every secret value into CI logs
advisory.suggested_fix: Only treat an Attribute receiver as consumed when the attr is a value-scoped accessor (e.g. `attr == 'get'`), and always treat os.environ as bare when it is the receiver of `.copy`/`.items`/`.values`/`.keys` calls that render full contents.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the detector (and add table cases) so `os.environ.copy()`, `os.environ.items()`, and `os.environ.keys()` used as assert operands are flagged, not sanctioned as consumed receivers.
evidence: `if isinstance(sub, (ast.Attribute, ast.Subscript)) and _is_os_environ(sub.value): consumed.add(id(sub.value))` — any receiver marks os.environ safe

For `assert "X" not in os.environ.copy()` the node `os.environ` is the `.value` of the `.copy` Attribute, so it is added to `consumed` and never flagged, yet `.copy()`/`.items()` render every value and `.keys()` every name

test_detector_sanctions_value_scoped_assertions parametrize only covers `os.environ.get(...)`, `os.environ[...]`, and the bool-bound form (lines 200-208); no parametrize case asserts `.copy()`/`.keys()`/`.items()` are flagged

ABSENCE: no test in the module asserts a receiver-shape that still leaks the environment is treated as a finding, so a future `assert ... not in os.environ.copy()` would pass test_no_assert_in_the_suite_renders_the_raw_environment
advisory.finding: The `os.environ`-audit detector treats every attribute/subscript receiver as 'consumed and safe', so leaking forms `os.environ.copy()`, `os.environ.items()`, and `os.environ.keys()` (which render environment contents as a comparison operand) are NOT flagged, and no test exercises them — the suite-wide audit cannot detect this regression class.
scenarios: A future test writes `assert "KEY" not in os.environ.copy()` — it leaks the full environment on failure but the audit reports zero offenders
advisory.suggested_fix: Restrict the consumed-receiver exemption to value-retrieving forms only: treat `os.environ` as consumed when it is the receiver of a subscript, or of `.get`/`.pop`/`.__getitem__` attribute access, but NOT of `.copy`/`.items`/`.keys`/`.values`; add positive parametrize cases for the leaking forms to test_detector_flags_a_rendered_environment.
